issue.title: False positive for myself
issue.body:
A bit of an unusual issue, but I'm actually here to report a false positive this time.

Agentscan recently started flagging me because my branch creation -> pr created time is low. https://agentscan.tools/user/dyc3

My most common method of creating prs is via the github cli, with `gh pr create`. More recently, I've also created stacked PRs with `gh stack submit`. Both methods handle pushing the branch and opening the PR, so of course it looks fast. 

What's confusing is that its only started flagging me today. I've been creating PRs with `gh pr create` for years, longer than agentscan has existed. So I was a bit surprised to see myself get flagged when it hasn't happened before.

issue.title: Detect undeclared custom Vue directives in noUndeclaredVariables

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Summary

Add support for reporting unresolved custom Vue directives in `noUndeclaredVariables`.

PR #11435 registers template references so `noUnusedVariables` and `noUnusedImports` recognise local bindings such as `vHighlight` used by `v-highlight`. It intentionally does not report missing custom directives.

## Rationale

A custom directive used in a Vue template can be unresolved. However, a directive can be registered through several mechanisms:

- a top-level binding, for example `const vHighlight = ...`;
- the component Options API, through `directives: { highlight: ... }`;
- global registration, through `app.directive("highlight", ...)`.

The implementation needs an architectural decision that prevents false positives for valid component-level and global registrations.

## Affected areas

- Vue template reference handling in `crates/biome_embeds`
- Vue directive syntax helpers in `crates/biome_html_syntax`
- `noUndeclaredVariables` analysis in `crates/biome_js_analyze`

## Acceptance criteria

- Define which directive registration mechanisms `noUndeclaredVariables` resolves.
- Report an undeclared custom directive when no supported registration exists.
- Do not report Vue built-in directives.
- Do not report custom directives registered through supported Options API or global mechanisms.
- Add fixtures and snapshot coverage for supported and unresolved directive cases.

## Backlinks

- Deferred from PR #11435: https://github.com/biomejs/biome/pull/11435
- Requested by @dyc3 in the PR discussion.

comment.body: For global definitions, they should be treated like global variables. Users should have to declare them as global variables in configuration. The options api needs to be handled. Composition api was handled in #11435

issue.title: feat: add native Jellyfin support
issue.body:
## What

Adds native Jellyfin video service support to OpenTogetherTube, allowing users to paste Jellyfin URLs directly into the room queue.

## Why

Previously, users had to manually construct HLS URLs and subtitle links. This provides a seamless experience similar to YouTube/Vimeo integration.

## Changes

### Server
- **New `jellyfin.ts` adapter**: Parses Jellyfin web UI, download, and HLS URLs. Extracts API keys from query params or hash fragments. Uses compound IDs (`serverOrigin::itemId`) for server identification.
- **Auth**: Sends X-Emby-* headers and X-Emby-Token for Jellyfin 10.11+ API compatibility. Caches user IDs per server+apiKey.
- **Video info**: Fetches item details via `/Users/{userId}/Items/{itemId}`, constructs HLS stream URLs, and extracts subtitles from PlaybackInfo API.
- **Series resolution**: Resolves series/season URLs to individual episode videos.
- **Config**: Added `jellyfin.instances` for server allowlist (empty = allow all).

### Client
- **HlsPlayer**: Rewrote caption handling to use native `<track>` elements instead of HLS.js subtitle tracks, enabling external subtitle injection. Added Jellyfin bitrate profiles and URL-based quality switching.
- **Quality**: Auto quality label now displays "Auto (X Mbps)" using the current MaxStreamingBitrate from the URL.
- **CC button**: Fixed to select track 0 on first press if no track was previously selected, remembering the last selection on subsequent toggles.
- **VideoSettings**: Added scrollable subtitle menu for long lists.

### Tests
- 31 unit tests covering URL parsing, API key extraction, video info fetching, series resolution, and auth headers.

issue.title: 💅 `useVueHyphenatedAttributes` flags colon-separated props

labels.name: repo-4d08208b
labels.description: Status: report has been confirmed as a valid bug

issue.body:
### Environment information

not applicable

### Rule name

useVueHyphenatedAttributes

### Playground link

https://biomejs.dev/playground/?lintRules=useVueHyphenatedAttributes&tab=formatter&pane=Diagnostics&files.package.&files.src%2FAppView.%3D

### Expected result

I expected it not to flag the props.

This style of props is for example used in one of Vue's biggest UI Libraries, Prime Vue. It is used for their [`pass through API`](https://primevue.org/passthrough/#declarative).

As far as I understand, the rule is supposed to flag all non-kebab-case props, e.g. `textColor` or `text_color`.

In the example, I would argue, all props are in kebab case (e.g. `pt:header:data-test-id`). Perhaps this could be considered a bug in which the rule judges the colons as invalid separators?

issue.title: useConsistentTestIt: safe fix renames a call whose callee is an imported binding, breaking the import

labels.name: repo-4d08208b
labels.description: Status: report has been confirmed as a valid bug

issue.body:
## Environment

Biome 2.5.7 (aqua-installed binary, macOS arm64).

## Summary

`nursery/useConsistentTestIt` classifies its fix as **safe**, but it
rewrites the *call* and leaves the *import* alone. When the callee is an
imported binding rather than a test-runner global, the safe fix produces
a module that throws on load.

The concrete case is `@fast-check/vitest`, which exports `test` (carrying
`.prop`) rather than relying on the vitest global.

## Reproduction

`biome.json`:

```json
{ "linter": { "rules": { "nursery": { "useConsistentTestIt": "on" } } } }
```

`a.test.ts`:

```ts
import { fc, test } from "@fast-check/vitest";

test.prop([fc.string()])("length is non-negative", (s) => s.length >= 0);
```

`biome check --write a.test.ts` produces:

```diff
-test.prop([fc.string()])("length is non-negative", (s) => s.length >= 0);
+it.prop([fc.string()])("length is non-negative", (s) => s.length >= 0);
```

The `import { fc, test }` line is untouched. `it` is the vitest global
and has no `.prop`, so the module throws when loaded and the test
silently stops existing. On a real suite this took 22 files / 337 tests
to 21 / 335, with nothing in the output indicating that a fixer had
removed test coverage.

## It is not about the preferred direction

Setting `options.function: "test"` produces the mirror image:

```ts
import { it } from "vitest";

it("x", () => {});
```

becomes

```ts
import { it } from "vitest";

test("x", () => {});
```

`it` is still imported and now unused, and `test` is not bound. So the
problem is not which name the rule prefers — it is that the rule renames
a call whose callee resolves to an **imported binding** without
considering, or updating, that binding.

## Expected

One of:

1. the rule does not fire when the callee resolves to an imported
   binding (it cannot know that the two names are interchangeable in
   that module), or
2. the fix is reclassified as **unsafe**, so `--write` leaves it alone
   and `--write --unsafe` is required, or
3. the fix updates the import alongside the call — only sound when the
   module actually exports both names.

Option 1 or 2 seems right; a rename that depends on a global being
present should not apply where the name is explicitly imported.

## Actual

The fix is classified `safe` and applied by `biome check --write`,
producing a module that throws at import time.

## Notes

The documentation states the rule addresses the fact that "`it` and
`test` are aliases for the same function in most test frameworks", which
holds for the globals but not for a package that exports one of the two
names with extra properties on it.

Happy to open a PR if a maintainer confirms which of the three
directions is preferred.

issue.title: 🐛 GritQL patterns for `export { ... } from ...` don't match multiple specifiers

labels.name: repo-4d08208b
labels.description: Status: report has been confirmed as a valid bug

issue.body:
### Environment information

<details>

```bash

CLI:
  Version:                      2.5.9
  Color support:                true

Platform:
  CPU Architecture:             aarch64
  OS:                           macos

Environment:
  BIOME_DISTRIBUTION:                npm
  BIOME_LOG_FILE:                    unset
  BIOME_LOG_PATH:                    unset
  BIOME_LOG_PREFIX_NAME:             unset
  BIOME_LOG_LEVEL:                   unset
  BIOME_LOG_KIND:                    unset
  BIOME_CONFIG_PATH:                 unset
  BIOME_THREADS:                     unset
  BIOME_WATCHER_KIND:                unset
  BIOME_WATCHER_POLLING_INTERVAL:    unset
  BIOME_BINARY:                      unset
  RUST_BACKTRACE:                    unset
  NO_COLOR:                     unset
  TERM:                         xterm-256color
  JS_RUNTIME_VERSION:           v24.18.0
  JS_RUNTIME_NAME:              node
  NODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER:         npm/11.16.0

Biome Configuration:
  Status:                       Loaded successfully.
  Path:                         biome.json
  Formatter enabled:            false
  Linter enabled:               true
  Assist enabled:               true
  VCS enabled:                  false
  HTML full support enabled:    unset

Workspace:
  Open Documents:               0

```

</details>


### What happened?

A GritQL pattern like `` `export { $specifiers } from $source` `` only matches named re-exports that
have exactly one plain specifier. Exports with two or more specifiers, an alias, or an inline `type`
modifier are not matched. `@getgrit/cli apply` matches all of them.

[Playground](https://biomejs.dev/playground/?tab=semantic-model&pane=GritQL&%3D&language=ts&gritQuery=or+%7B%0A++%60export+%7B+%24specifiers+%7D+from+%24source%60%2C%0A%7D)

```ts
export { hoge } from "a" // works
export { hoge as h } from "b" // CURRENTLY DOES NOT WORK
export { hoge, fuga } from "d" // CURRENTLY DOES NOT WORK
export { type hoge, fuga } from "e" // CURRENTLY DOES NOT WORK
```


| code | @getgrit/cli  | biome 2.5.9|
|--|--|--|
|export { hoge } from 'a'|⚪︎|⚪︎|
|export { hoge as h } from 'b'|⚪︎ |×|
|export { type hoge } from 'c'|⚪︎ |×|
|export { hoge, fuga } from 'd'|⚪︎ |×|
|export { type hoge, fuga } from 'e'|⚪︎ |×|

### Expected result

they all should be matched

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow Biome's Code of Conduct

issue.title: useConsistentTestIt: safe fix renames a call whose callee is an imported binding, breaking the import

labels.name: repo-4d08208b
labels.description: Status: report has been confirmed as a valid bug

issue.body:
## Environment

Biome 2.5.7 (aqua-installed binary, macOS arm64).

## Summary

`nursery/useConsistentTestIt` classifies its fix as **safe**, but it
rewrites the *call* and leaves the *import* alone. When the callee is an
imported binding rather than a test-runner global, the safe fix produces
a module that throws on load.

The concrete case is `@fast-check/vitest`, which exports `test` (carrying
`.prop`) rather than relying on the vitest global.

## Reproduction

`biome.json`:

```json
{ "linter": { "rules": { "nursery": { "useConsistentTestIt": "on" } } } }
```

`a.test.ts`:

```ts
import { fc, test } from "@fast-check/vitest";

test.prop([fc.string()])("length is non-negative", (s) => s.length >= 0);
```

`biome check --write a.test.ts` produces:

```diff
-test.prop([fc.string()])("length is non-negative", (s) => s.length >= 0);
+it.prop([fc.string()])("length is non-negative", (s) => s.length >= 0);
```

The `import { fc, test }` line is untouched. `it` is the vitest global
and has no `.prop`, so the module throws when loaded and the test
silently stops existing. On a real suite this took 22 files / 337 tests
to 21 / 335, with nothing in the output indicating that a fixer had
removed test coverage.

## It is not about the preferred direction

Setting `options.function: "test"` produces the mirror image:

```ts
import { it } from "vitest";

it("x", () => {});
```

becomes

```ts
import { it } from "vitest";

test("x", () => {});
```

`it` is still imported and now unused, and `test` is not bound. So the
problem is not which name the rule prefers — it is that the rule renames
a call whose callee resolves to an **imported binding** without
considering, or updating, that binding.

## Expected

One of:

1. the rule does not fire when the callee resolves to an imported
   binding (it cannot know that the two names are interchangeable in
   that module), or
2. the fix is reclassified as **unsafe**, so `--write` leaves it alone
   and `--write --unsafe` is required, or
3. the fix updates the import alongside the call — only sound when the
   module actually exports both names.

Option 1 or 2 seems right; a rename that depends on a global being
present should not apply where the name is explicitly imported.

## Actual

The fix is classified `safe` and applied by `biome check --write`,
producing a module that throws at import time.

## Notes

The documentation states the rule addresses the fact that "`it` and
`test` are aliases for the same function in most test frameworks", which
holds for the globals but not for a package that exports one of the two
names with extra properties on it.

Happy to open a PR if a maintainer confirms which of the three
directions is preferred.

## Summary

Hello, I'm Erika from the Astro team, again.

This PR is very similar to a fix that was done in https://github.com/biomejs/biome/pull/11403, except it fixes a slightly different case, expressions that *only* contain comments.

Code was generated using the help of AI agents. Claude Opus 5 was used for the code, and Claude Fable 5 was used for an adversarial review of all the commits of this and associated PR. Finally, code has been read and reviewed by a human (once again, probably the weakest link in this chain,)

Closes https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/8294

Added some tests

N/A. I think Astro users would expect all of these to work!

comment.body: i think there's an issue somewhere about this. if there is, we should mention it in the changeset
String error type doesn't seem like the right choice

This is very hacky, you shouldn't be using `new_raw`.

We likely need to consider some parser changes or changes to the embedded bindings/references services to properly handle this.

honestly, not entirely sure right now. its real wrench in the gears that it requires the kebab to camel case conversion.

- Storing the string isn't ideal because it would be a string allocation every time you use the directive
- Storing metadata about the case conversion also isn't ideal because the naive way to implement it requires doing the case conversion multiple times

It might be possible to mitigate the downsides of those approaches by leaning into salsa a bit more. I'd have to think about it.

## Summary

Closes https://github.com/biomejs/biome/discussions/6265

From here on, `npm` is used as "npm registry".

A long time has passed since we launched grit plugins, and we have received enough feedback. So I decided we could use `npm` to distribute and load grit (and future JS) plugins. 

One [feedback](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/discussions/6265#discussioncomment-16918562) thread stood out to me, and it's essentially about the enterprise setting. 

Plus, we already support loading configuration files via `npm`, so I don't see any "conflict of interest" in loading plugins from `npm` too.

___

> [!NOTE]
> Code designed by me and implemented via a coding agent.

- There's now a `biome-manifest.json` file that plugin authors need to create at the root of their package, which is used to declare the grit files to load.
- The `biome-manifest.json` file is now deserialised during the `lint` pass in the `json.rs` file, same as the configuration file.
- The plugin cache has been redesigned. Before, it used the path as key, but now that doesn't work anymore because we have overrides and package paths.
- The plugin loader now uses our `biome_resolver` to load the manifest and the grit files (designed to import JS files too)

@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+---
+"@biomejs/biome": patch
+---
+
+Fixed `{#`, `{/`, `{:` and `{@` being read as Svelte block openings in every HTML-like file. They are now Svelte-only, so in HTML, Vue and Angular files a sequence such as `{#if x}` is ordinary text instead of a parse error.
comment.body: It's true that normally we do want to use Syntax Feature's `parse_exclusive_syntax`, but HTML is a bit more nuanced because usually syntax that applies to one framework becomes plain text in another. So yes, this is fine.

comment.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,41 @@
+---
+"@biomejs/biome": minor
+---
+
+Added support for loading Grit plugins from npm packages.
+
+Plugin authors can distribute their rules by including a mandatory `biome-manifest.json` or `biome-manifest.jsonc` in their library, which will look like this:
+
+```json
+{
+  "$schema": "./node_modules/@biomejs/biome/manifest_schema.json",
+  "version": 1,
+  "rules": ["rules/noDeprecatedApi.grit", "rules/useCompanyLogger.grit"]
+}
+```
+
+The package **must** publish the manifest and the rule files, for example, with the `files` field in `package.json`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "name": "@scope/biome-plugin",
+  "files": ["biome-manifest.json", "rules"]
+}
+```

issue.title: 🐛 Svelte: Components could be promoted as import types

labels.name: repo-4d08208b
labels.description: Status: report has been confirmed as a valid bug

issue.body:
### Environment information

<details>

```bash
CLI:
  Version:                      2.5.8
  Color support:                true

Platform:
  CPU Architecture:             x86_64
  OS:                           linux

Environment:
  BIOME_DISTRIBUTION:                npm
  BIOME_LOG_PATH:                    unset
  BIOME_LOG_PREFIX_NAME:             unset
  BIOME_LOG_LEVEL:                   unset
  BIOME_LOG_KIND:                    unset
  BIOME_CONFIG_PATH:                 unset
  BIOME_THREADS:                     unset
  BIOME_WATCHER_KIND:                unset
  BIOME_WATCHER_POLLING_INTERVAL:    unset
  NO_COLOR:                     unset
  TERM:                         xterm-ghostty
  JS_RUNTIME_VERSION:           v26.7.0
  JS_RUNTIME_NAME:              node
  NODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER:         pnpm/11.3.0

Biome Configuration:
  Status:                       Loaded successfully.
  Path:                         biome.json
  Formatter enabled:            true
  Linter enabled:               true
  Assist enabled:               true
  VCS enabled:                  true
  HTML full support enabled:    true

Workspace:
  Open Documents:               0
```

</details>


### What happened?

In Svelte, components are promoted as import types when there is a variable of that component type, even if it's used.

- ~~The linter raises a warn/err~~
- The analyzer auto fix adds `type`, and breaks the build

Before:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import Modal from "$lib/components/Modal.svelte"

  let myModal: Modal

</script>

<Modal bind:this={myModal}>
</Modal>
```

After auto fix:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import type Modal from "$lib/components/Modal.svelte"

  let myModal: Modal

</script>

<Modal bind:this={myModal}>
</Modal>
```

Workaround:

```json
  "linter": {
    "enabled": true,
    "rules": {
      "preset": "recommended",
      "style": {
        "useImportType": "off"
      }
    }
  },
```

https://biomejs.dev/playground/?lineWidth=100&indentStyle=space&trailingCommas=es5&indentWidth=4&semicolons=as-needed&indentScriptAndStyle=true&lintRules=all&tab=analyzer-fixes&pane=Diagnostics&%2BAAoAPAAvAE0AbwBkAGEAbAA%2BAA%3D%3D&language=svelte


### Expected result

Do not consider as import types when a component is used.

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow Biome's Code of Conduct

labels.name: repo-4d08208b
labels.description: Status: report has been confirmed as a valid bug

issue.body:
### Environment information

<details>

```bash
CLI:
  Version:                      2.5.8
  Color support:                true

Platform:
  CPU Architecture:             x86_64
  OS:                           linux

Environment:
  BIOME_DISTRIBUTION:                npm
  BIOME_LOG_PATH:                    unset
  BIOME_LOG_PREFIX_NAME:             unset
  BIOME_LOG_LEVEL:                   unset
  BIOME_LOG_KIND:                    unset
  BIOME_CONFIG_PATH:                 unset
  BIOME_THREADS:                     unset
  BIOME_WATCHER_KIND:                unset
  BIOME_WATCHER_POLLING_INTERVAL:    unset
  NO_COLOR:                     unset
  TERM:                         xterm-ghostty
  JS_RUNTIME_VERSION:           v26.7.0
  JS_RUNTIME_NAME:              node
  NODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER:         pnpm/11.3.0

Biome Configuration:
  Status:                       Loaded successfully.
  Path:                         biome.json
  Formatter enabled:            true
  Linter enabled:               true
  Assist enabled:               true
  VCS enabled:                  true
  HTML full support enabled:    true

Workspace:
  Open Documents:               0
```

</details>


### What happened?

In Svelte, components are promoted as import types when there is a variable of that component type, even if it's used.

- ~~The linter raises a warn/err~~
- The analyzer auto fix adds `type`, and breaks the build

Before:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import Modal from "$lib/components/Modal.svelte"

  let myModal: Modal

</script>

<Modal bind:this={myModal}>
</Modal>
```

After auto fix:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import type Modal from "$lib/components/Modal.svelte"

  let myModal: Modal

</script>

<Modal bind:this={myModal}>
</Modal>
```

Workaround:

```json
  "linter": {
    "enabled": true,
    "rules": {
      "preset": "recommended",
      "style": {
        "useImportType": "off"
      }
    }
  },
```

https://biomejs.dev/playground/?lineWidth=100&indentStyle=space&trailingCommas=es5&indentWidth=4&semicolons=as-needed&indentScriptAndStyle=true&lintRules=all&tab=analyzer-fixes&pane=Diagnostics&%2BAAoAPAAvAE0AbwBkAGEAbAA%2BAA%3D%3D&language=svelte


### Expected result

Do not consider as import types when a component is used.

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow Biome's Code of Conduct

comment.body: Your playground doesn't reproduce the bug. I'm also confused because your `biome rage` output shows you have html full support enabled, so you shouldn't be seeing this bug in the first place.

issue.title: 💅 `useImportExtensions` with `forceJsExtensions` rewrites `.json` and `.css` imports to `.js`
issue.body:
### Environment information

<details>

```bash
CLI:
  Version:                      2.5.8
  Color support:                true

Platform:
  CPU Architecture:             x86_64
  OS:                           linux

Environment:
  BIOME_DISTRIBUTION:                npm
  BIOME_LOG_PATH:                    unset
  BIOME_LOG_PREFIX_NAME:             unset
  BIOME_LOG_LEVEL:                   unset
  BIOME_LOG_KIND:                    unset
  BIOME_CONFIG_PATH:                 unset
  BIOME_THREADS:                     unset
  BIOME_WATCHER_KIND:                unset
  BIOME_WATCHER_POLLING_INTERVAL:    unset
  NO_COLOR:                     unset
  TERM:                         xterm-ghostty
  JS_RUNTIME_VERSION:           v24.18.0
  JS_RUNTIME_NAME:              node
  NODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER:         bun/1.3.14

Biome Configuration:
  Status:                       Loaded successfully.
  Path:                         biome.json
  Formatter enabled:            true
  Linter enabled:               true
  Assist enabled:               true
  VCS enabled:                  false
  HTML full support enabled:    unset

Linter:
  JavaScript enabled:           unset
  JSON enabled:                 unset
  CSS enabled:                  unset
  GraphQL enabled:              unset
  Recommended:                  unset
  Enabled rules:
    correctness/useImportExtensions

Workspace:
  Open Documents:               0
```

</details>

### Rule name

`correctness/useImportExtensions`, with `forceJsExtensions: true`

### Playground link

https://github.com/AlbinoGeek/biome-json-import-repro

Not a playground link: the rule only fires when the import resolves on disk, and the
playground's linter panel exposes presets and domains but not per-rule options, so
`forceJsExtensions` cannot be set there.

```
npm install
npx biome check --write cases.ts
node cases.ts
```

Relative imports that already carry a non-script extension are rewritten:

- `./data.json` → `./data.js`
- `./style.css` → `./style.js`

The fix is classified **safe**, so `check --write` applies it without `--unsafe`, and the
imports stop resolving:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../data.js'
```

Bisected on the same `cases.ts` and `biome.json`, only the version varies:

```
2.1.4 .. 2.2.4   .json / .css untouched
2.2.5 .. 2.5.8   both rewritten to .js
```

2.2.4 already honoured `forceJsExtensions`, rewriting an extensionless `./mod` to
`./mod.js`, so this is not the option first landing. 2.2.5 added rewriting imports that
already had an extension.

#7734 is the same bug. It was closed when `extensionMappings` landed, but that is a
separate option; `forceJsExtensions` still behaves this way in 2.5.8.

### Expected result

Only `.ts` / `.tsx` map to `.js`. `.json` and `.css` imports are left alone, as in 2.2.4.

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow Biome's Code of Conduct

comment.body: yes. use `extensionMappings` instead of `forceJsExtensions` if you don't like the latter's behavior.
